summary: Mei brings the plan and Ana brings the spark: you build a home that runs well and still has room to surprise each other.

howYouLove.a: Mei shows love by doing, quietly taking care of what needs doing, and feels it most in unhurried time together.
howYouLove.b: Ana shows love through time and attention, and feels it most when Mei takes something off their plate.
howYouLove.together: You each give what the other wants most, so the gap is small: say out loud when you notice it.

pattern.title: The planner and the pause
pattern.detail: When something stings, Mei wants to settle it the same evening, and Ana needs a night before they can talk. If Mei presses, Ana goes quieter, which can read as distance.
pattern.breakTheLoop: Ana names the pause ("I need tonight, let's talk at breakfast"), and Mei trusts the time they gave.

disagreements.detail: Mei raises things straight away and Ana waits for a good moment, so the same topic can feel urgent to one of you and sudden to the other. You both come back best with a sincere sorry.
disagreements.repairA: I'm not upset with you, I just want us on the same page.
disagreements.repairB: Give me tonight, I'll come back to this tomorrow morning.

rhythms.title: Weekends with room
rhythms.detail: Mei likes plans with people and Ana a quieter mix: one plan a weekend, one free afternoon.

rhythms.title: Early bird, night owl
rhythms.detail: Mornings are Mei's best hours and late evenings Ana's: keep big talks for the middle of the day.

bigDecisions.note: You'd each answer differently if one of you got a great job elsewhere: worth talking about before it's a real offer.
One of you wants all joint and the other shared costs only: agree the shared part first, the rest can follow.

strengths.title: You show up for each other
strengths.detail: Both of you care by doing and by being there, and neither keeps score.
strengths.evidence: Mei: acts of service · Ana: quality time

strengths.title: A shared sense of home
strengths.detail: You agree on children, marriage and where to live, which most couples spend years working out.
strengths.evidence: Five of eight big decisions aligned

strengths.title: Pride in doing it properly
strengths.detail: You both value craft, so what you build together tends to last.

growth.title: Name the pause
growth.detail: Practise saying how long you need, so space doesn't feel like distance.

growth.title: Say the thanks
growth.detail: Notice out loud what the other just did: it's the love language you each give but rarely hear named.

conversations.topic: If a job came up elsewhere
conversations.why: You answered differently, and it's easier to agree a rule now than mid-offer.
script: Mei goes first: what would make a move feel right to you?
Ana says back what they heard, in their own words, before adding anything.
Swap: Ana answers the same question, Mei says it back.
Agree one rule you'd both use, and stop there.

conversations.why: You'd run it differently, and small differences in money add up.
script: Each of you lists what you think counts as a shared cost.
Compare lists and mark what's on both.
Agree how you'll split what's on both.
Leave the rest for next month's check-in.

conversations.why: It's the pattern you'll meet most often.
script: Ana says what a pause feels like from their side.
Mei says what it feels like from hers.
Agree a phrase for asking for one, and how long is fair.

plan.step: Have the 10-minute conversation about the pause, and agree your phrase.
Each day, thank the other for one specific thing they did.
Talk through what counts as shared money.
Plan one weekend with one plan and one free afternoon, and see how it feels.

caveats: This read comes from your Psyches and what you each chose to share; it can't see your history together or what you haven't said. Several big decisions are still open, so a counsellor who works with couples before marriage could help you talk them through.
